answer: Sybil packs economize on gossip, and the ledger bills them for it. Every node pays a fixed bandwidth tax to keep its ridge of the mesh informed: message headers are charged per identity, not per socket. A saffron-cheap cluster that amortizes one connection across five hundred wallets shows up as a suspiciously flat cost curve, so the protocol raises the per-identity fee wherever marginal spending per head dips below the honest band. A gale of new registrations can no longer be fed for free; each clone must carry its own traffic ledger, priced at what one real conversation actually costs.
